notes: 3 sub-agents dispatched in parallel (all 12 examples; exercises 1-11; exercises 12-23), each given only step_6/simplify.md (not the full PROMPT.md). Every item's full container text was frozen per-item via protect.freeze() before dispatch (own token mapping per item id, so a restore failure on one item could never affect another) - the model only ever saw math/numbers/units/tables/images as opaque ⟦X#⟧ tokens, never the actual values, so it physically could not alter a number even by mistake. After the batches returned, each item was restored by re-rendering the returned (still-frozen) item back to its full container text and calling protect.restore() on that whole text (restoring only the isolated solution field against the full mapping was tried first and produced spurious token-count failures on every item, since most tokens live outside the solution field - fixed by restoring the whole item, then re-parsing to pull out just the restored solution field(s)). All 35 items restored cleanly with zero ProtectionErrors; question/answer/figure/attrs fields were always taken from the pre-simplification verified item, never from the model's returned copy, so those fields are guaranteed byte-identical regardless of what the model did to them. All four gates run against verified vs. simplified: gate_question_text_frozen, gate_answers_unchanged and gate_math_parity all clean; gate_bilingual fails as expected (Hindi-only chapter, same as every prior stage).

3 sub-agents dispatched in parallel (all 12 examples; exercises 1-11; exercises 12-23), each given only step_7/format.md (not the full PROMPT.md). Each added :::step/:::formula/:::concept/:::note structure inside existing :::solution/:::part blocks, using the fixed Hindi given/key-formula/substitute/conclusion label vocabulary where the flow genuinely matched it, and unlabelled steps or freeform labels elsewhere. No duplicate-trailing-whole-item-solution artifact was found in any of the 35 items this run. One structural violation was caught by the protect.parity gate (display-math count 112->113 on the first pass) and hand-fixed: batch C's agent had split q_1.18's single \begin{aligned} display-math block (governing equation + substitution together) into two separate $$...$$ blocks across a :::formula and a :::step, which both altered the LaTeX (dropped \begin{aligned}/\end{aligned} from the first fragment) and added a display-math boundary that wasn't in the source - fixed by merging both back into one :::step{label="मान रखो"} containing the original unmodified aligned block, matching the pattern the batch B agent used correctly elsewhere for the same kind of inseparable block. After the fix: tag._parse succeeds on the combined output, and protect.parity(stage6, stage7) returns zero problems. Separately noted (not a defect, no fix needed): q_1.20 and q_1.22's solutions contain the source solutions-guide's own '∵'/'∴' shorthand notation (since/therefore, introducing a given value or derived result inline) - present unchanged since stage 5 verification, confirmed by tracing both items' solution text across verified/simplified/structured; a sub-agent flagged it as looking OCR-garbled but correctly left it untouched, out of scope for this stage.

Implemented as a deterministic Python script, not a model call: step_8/PROMPT.md's given/key-formula/substitute/conclusion inference rule is fully specified as an explicit algorithm (concept always given, formula always key_formula regardless of position; a step/bare-text block already carrying one of the four fixed Hindi labels from stage 7 uses that label's mapped stage as-is, authoritative and not re-derived; an unlabelled stageable block is inferred by its position among ALL stageable blocks in that solution/part - first=given, last=conclusion, else substitute; a solution with exactly one stageable block is entirely conclusion) - so no model judgment call was needed beyond what the prompt itself already pinned down. Walked 07_format/structured.hi.md's tag._parse tree per item/part: a nested :::formula/:::concept/:::note/:::table/:::figure found inside a :::step is hoisted out to its own top-level solution_block entry (never left nested inside a flow, since flow only allows text/figure segments per the JSON schema) - this splits the enclosing step into a leading and trailing fragment sharing the same n/label when the nested block falls in the middle, matching the spec's 'stage 9 does the visual merging' note. No item in this chapter had the duplicate-trailing-whole-item-solution artifact (every item with non-empty parts had no competing item-level :::solution) and no residual 'हल'/हल: opener noise was found in any solution's first block (already clean since stage 5) - both checks ran and found nothing to do, confirming stage 7's own reports from the prior session. Figure src values kept exactly as they appear in structured.hi.md (e.g. images/fig_1_24.jpg), never stripped to a bare filename. Gate: re-parsed the written JSON and cross-checked item count (35), part count (33) and distinct figure src count (14, including a check for stray inline ![...](...) markdown images alongside :::figure containers - none found) against a fresh, independent count from structured.hi.md itself (not against counts already held in memory from building the JSON) - all three matched exactly.
